names.official: Income tax on individuals, State part (national tax on personal income and surtax)
names.native: Toppskatt og trinnskatt (statlig skatt på personinntekt)

taxes.base: Personal income (wages, pensions, self-employment): the bracket tax and the national insurance contribution are charged on it; general income (including capital income) is taxed at a flat rate.

rate.headline: 22% on general income; bracket tax on personal income
details: General income is taxed at a flat 22%; personal income is charged the bracket tax and the employee’s national insurance contribution (PwC; rates for 2026).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of June to September 2026), not checked against the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten).

instruments.explanation: The National Tax List gives two lines for the income tax of individuals (NOK 506 billion in all). Eurostat’s accounts place NOK 240 billion of it with the municipalities and counties and the rest with the State. This row is the State’s part.
exceptions: The list’s figures for the largest Norwegian taxes are rounded values (for example NOK 350,000 and 156,000 million).

names.official: Net wealth tax, State part

taxes.base: The net wealth of individuals and households (NOK 31.1 billion) and corporations (NOK 1.1 billion).

rate.headline: Set by the Storting each year
details: The rate and the thresholds are not extracted here.

instruments.explanation: The list gives NOK 32,200 million for the net wealth tax in all; Eurostat’s accounts place NOK 21,500 million of it with the municipalities and counties and the rest with the State.

legalRefs.locator: sheet NO, D59A C01 and C02

names.official: Corporate income tax

taxes.base: Net income of companies, apart from the petroleum sector, which has its own tax.

rate.headline: 22% (25% in parts of the financial sector)
details: CIT is in general assessed at 22%; certain companies within the financial sector pay 25% (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of June to September 2026), not checked against the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten).

instruments.explanation: NOK 109.5 billion in 2024 (a rounded figure in the list).

names.official: Ordinary income tax on petroleum revenue and special tax on petroleum income
names.native: Ordinær skatt og særskatt på petroleumsinntekt

taxes.base: Net income from the extraction and pipeline transport of petroleum on the Norwegian continental shelf: ordinary income tax NOK 100 billion and the special tax NOK 281 billion in the list.

rate.headline: 78% marginal: 22% ordinary + 56% special
details: Taxation is based on net income at a marginal rate of 78%, made up of the ordinary 22% corporate rate and a 56% special tax (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of June to September 2026), not checked against the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten).

instruments.explanation: NOK 381 billion in 2024, about as much as the VAT (NOK 390 billion). These are rounded values in the list.

names.official: Special tax on hydroelectric income and special tax on aquaculture income

taxes.base: Hydropower income (NOK 15.5 billion) and aquaculture income (NOK 2.0 billion) as named in the National Tax List.

instruments.explanation: Two sector taxes.

legalRefs.locator: sheet NO, D51B C02 and C05

names.official: Tax on dividends paid to foreign shareholders and taxes paid by residents of Svalbard
names.native: Kildeskatt på utbytte til utenlandske aksjonærer; Svalbard

taxes.base: Dividends paid to foreign shareholders (NOK 13.4 billion) and the tax on residents and corporations of Svalbard (NOK 0.2 billion).

instruments.explanation: Two lines.

names.official: Employers’ social security contributions (National Insurance, the Public Service Pension Fund and the seamen’s scheme)

taxes.base: Employees’ gross salary. National Insurance NOK 267.9 billion, the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund NOK 26.5 billion and the seamen’s pension arrangement NOK 0.9 billion.

rate.headline: 0% to 14.1%, by municipality
details: The employers’ contribution rate varies between 0% and 14.1% depending on the municipality of the head office; paid bimonthly (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of June to September 2026), not checked against the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten).

instruments.explanation: The largest line after the VAT, with different rates in different parts of the country.

names.official: Employees’ social security contributions (National Insurance, Public Service Pension Fund, seamen and fishermen)

taxes.base: Personal income. National Insurance NOK 155.4 billion, Public Service Pension Fund NOK 5.7 billion, seamen and fishermen small lines.

rate.headline: A percentage of personal income
details: The rate is not extracted here.

instruments.explanation: NOK 161.7 billion.

names.official: Contributions of the self-employed and of pensioners to the National Insurance

taxes.base: The self-employed (NOK 17.1 billion) and pensioners (NOK 15.6 billion).

instruments.explanation: Norwegian pensioners also pay a contribution on their pensions.

names.official: Value added tax

taxes.base: Goods and services supplied in Norway and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and claim input credits.

rate.headline: 25% general; 15% on food; 12% on transport and others
details: The general VAT rate is 25%; a reduced 15% applies to food and beverages (excluding alcohol, medication and tap water); lower rates apply to some services (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of June to September 2026), not checked against the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten).

instruments.explanation: NOK 390 billion, a rounded value in the list.

names.official: Customs duties

taxes.base: Imported goods.

rate.headline: Set by the Customs Tariff
details: Norway is outside the EU and keeps its customs revenue; Eurostat books it under central government.

instruments.explanation: NOK 3.6 billion.

names.official: Taxes on petrol, diesel, CO₂, NOx, greenhouse gases and lubricating oils, including the CO₂ and NOx taxes of the petroleum sector

taxes.base: Petrol (NOK 3.5 billion), diesel (NOK 6.7 billion), CO₂ emissions outside the petroleum sector (NOK 16.3 billion), CO₂ in the petroleum sector (NOK 7.8 billion), NOx, HFC and PFC gases, SF6, lubricating oils, sulphur and the road tax on natural gas.

rate.headline: Per litre or per tonne of emissions
details: The rates are not extracted here.

instruments.explanation: Eleven lines that the list books among taxes on products and pollution.

names.official: Tax on electricity (including the part paid to the Norwegian Energy Fund)

taxes.base: Electricity consumed: NOK 9.7 billion, and NOK 0.7 billion for the Norwegian Energy Fund.

instruments.explanation: Two lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet NO, D214A C04 and C05

names.official: Taxes on alcohol and on tobacco goods, and the tax on the turnover of tobacco products

taxes.base: Alcohol (NOK 16.5 billion), tobacco goods (NOK 7.8 billion) and a small tax on tobacco turnover.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Per litre of alcohol; per unit of tobacco

instruments.explanation: Three lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet NO, D214A C16 and C17, D29E C09

names.official: Taxes on beverage packaging, sugar, pharmaceutical products, waste incineration and pesticides
names.common: Packaging, sugar and other product taxes

taxes.base: Beverage packaging (NOK 3.0 billion in two lines), waste incineration (NOK 0.6 billion), pharmaceutical products and pharmacies (NOK 0.5 billion in four lines), sugar (NOK 0.2 billion) and pesticides.
taxes.payer: Producers, importers and sellers of the products.

instruments.explanation: Nine small product taxes.

names.official: Stamp duty on real estate transfers

taxes.base: The price of real estate on transfer.

rate.headline: A percentage of the price
details: The rate is not extracted here.

instruments.explanation: NOK 12.7 billion.

names.official: Motor vehicle registration tax, annual taxes on motor vehicles (weight-based, enterprises and households) and re-registration tax

taxes.base: Registration (NOK 7.9 billion), the annual tax paid by households (NOK 8.8 billion), by enterprises (NOK 1.8 billion), the weight-based tax (NOK 0.3 billion) and re-registration (NOK 1.8 billion).

instruments.explanation: Five lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet NO, D214D C01, D29B C01–C03, D59D C01

names.official: Tax on air traffic passengers

taxes.base: Passengers on flights from Norwegian airports.

instruments.explanation: NOK 2.2 billion.

names.official: Income from the state gaming company (Norsk Tipping)

taxes.base: The surplus of the State’s gaming monopoly.

instruments.explanation: NOK 6.9 billion, booked as the profits of a fiscal monopoly.

names.official: Financial activity tax on salary

taxes.base: The wage base of entities that mainly provide VAT-exempt financial services.

rate.headline: 5% of the wage base
details: Entities within the financial services sector are subject to a special payroll tax of 5% on the wage base (PwC).
As summarised by PwC (reviews of June to September 2026), not checked against the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten).

instruments.explanation: NOK 2.8 billion.

names.official: Levies on fish production, meat and eggs, milk and grain, fishing industry products and research in agriculture and fisheries, aquaculture control, and others
names.native: Avgifter på fiskeri, landbruk og havbruk

taxes.base: Excise duties on fish production (NOK 1.4 billion), market regulation levies on meat, eggs, milk, grain and furs (NOK 0.7 billion), the fishing industry product tax (NOK 0.6 billion), export duties for fisheries research (NOK 0.5 billion), research taxes in fisheries (NOK 0.4 billion) and agriculture (NOK 0.2 billion), wild marine resources (NOK 0.1 billion) and small lines.
taxes.payer: Producers and exporters in agriculture, fisheries and aquaculture.

instruments.explanation: Ten lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet NO, D29H C01, C03, C06, C08, C09, D29C C01, D214K, D29F C07–C08, D29E C08

names.official: Sector fees to regulators, customs quota auctions, tonnage tax, licences and other small lines

taxes.base: Sector fees to the Norwegian Communications Authority, the Water Resources and Energy Directorate, the Petroleum Safety Authority and the Metrology Service, the tonnage tax for shipping companies, proceeds from auctioning customs quotas, fishing and hunting licences, a tax on cinemas, the Svalbard environmental fund and the remainder of the inheritance and gift tax (NOK 30 million).

instruments.explanation: Eleven small lines, together under 0.2% of the total.

legalRefs.locator: sheet NO, D29H, D29E C06, D214E C02, D59F, D91A C01

names.official: Local and regional income tax on individuals (municipalities and counties)
names.native: Kommuneskatt og fylkesskatt (skatt på alminnelig inntekt)

taxes.base: The same general income as the State’s part of the tax, taxed in the municipality of residence.

rate.headline: Part of the 22% on general income
details: General income is taxed at a flat 22% (PwC); the municipalities and counties receive the largest part of that tax. The split between them is not extracted here.

instruments.explanation: NOK 240 billion: the main revenue source of the local level in the list.

names.official: Net wealth tax, part recorded under local government

taxes.base: The same net wealth as the State’s part.

rate.headline: Set by the Storting each year

instruments.explanation: Most of the net wealth tax is recorded under the municipalities and counties in Eurostat’s accounts.

names.official: Real estate tax

taxes.base: The assessed value of homes and other property in the municipalities that levy it.

rate.headline: Set by each municipality within a ceiling
details: The list does not give rates.

instruments.explanation: NOK 17.5 billion; municipalities decide whether to levy it.

names.official: Natural resource tax

taxes.base: Hydropower production, charged on the plants’ output.

rate.headline: Set by law
details: NOK 1.6 billion; Eurostat books the same amount under local government.

instruments.explanation: Revenue from power plants goes to the municipalities and counties where they are located.
